summary.title: Test Sizes
summary.one_liner: Google's Testing Blog post proposes classifying tests by "size" (Small, Medium, Large) based on constraints like isolation and runtime, rather than by names such as unit, integration, or end-to-end.
takeaways: Tests can be classified by size (Small, Medium, Large) using concrete criteria instead of ambiguous names like end-to-end or functional test.
A Small test roughly corresponds to a unit test, and a Large test to an end-to-end or system test, according to the post as quoted in the comments.
Test isolation constraints can conflict with medium and large web tests, which often depend on shared state from earlier steps.
Commenters debate whether test dependencies conflict with parallelism, with TestNG cited as a tool that supports dependencies in Selenium tests.
Commenters note that the size categories overlap with ISTQB glossary terms and question whether runtime limits such as 60 seconds are practical.
summary.summary: The post by Simon Stewart asks what to call tests that exercise an application through its UI, and argues that names like end-to-end, functional, or system test are ambiguous. It proposes grouping tests by size, using measurable criteria such as isolation and runtime limits. The page is mostly reader comments, which discuss test dependencies in Selenium with TestNG, parallelism, the ISTQB glossary, and whether a 60-second unit test limit is realistic. The visible text does not include the full size definitions, so the exact criteria are only partly shown.
